alex: Ran an nsys capture of the vLLM + TensorRT call path during a small-scale load test. Quick notes incoming, uploading trace now.

perfbot: profile uploaded: https://internal.redwood/profiles/1932101111.nsys :eyes: 

maya: grabbed the trace — high-level question: where in the callpath is most GPU time going? I see unexpected host<->device churn in the timeline.

alex: confirmed hotspots from the first pass: 1) lots of tiny cudaMemcpyAsync bursts during kvcache prewarm in the wrapper 2) scheduler spin/accept loop in vLLM consuming ~10-15ms total per second 3) many short-lived TRT kernels (kv_pack, transpose/permute helpers) that are sub-ms but extremely frequent.

jordan: can you paste the nsys invocation you used and the top kernel breakdown?

alex: ran: ```bash
nsys profile --sample=none -o /tmp/trace.nsys --trace=cuda,cudnn --duration=60 ./bin/serve --profile-mode
```
Top GPU time (rough from nsys summary):
- cudaMemcpyAsync: ~22%
- trt::gemm_fp16: ~19%
- trt::kv_pack / kv_pack_kernel: ~12%
- scheduler_spin / host-side enqueue: ~8%
- elementwise / small transpose kernels: ~7%

maya: memcpy that high suggests per-request small transfers. Are we prewarming kvcache per request?

alex: yes, current wrapper does a conservative per-request prewarm for the first 1-2 tokens to populate device KV. It issues multiple small async memcpys (2-8KB) per request which shows up as many discrete memcpy ops.

jordan: that pattern will kill throughput. Options: 1) aggregate prewarm memcpys across requests 2) use a pinned staging buffer to consolidate transfers 3) increase batching window slightly to let multiple requests share the same prewarm.

maya: tried a prototype (branch: reduce-kv-chatter) that coalesces per-request small memcpys into a single memcpy per scheduling tick. Short microbench: memcpy GPU time reduced ~60%, overall p99 latency improved ~8% under synthetic load.

alex: nice. pasted a small excerpt from the GPU timeline for context:
```text
[nsys timeline sample]
0.000us - cudaMemcpyAsync 4KB (prewarm)
0.120us - trt::kv_pack kernel
0.140us - cudaMemcpyAsync 3KB (prewarm)
0.260us - trt::transpose_rotary
0.310us - small elementwise kernel
0.380us - cudaMemcpyAsync 6KB (prewarm)
...
```

ops-bot: CI/build 2026-03-16T10:12 deployed to staging :white_check_mark:

maya: next investigation steps I propose: 1) add a 0.5ms batching window in the scheduler to allow prewarm aggregation, 2) move prewarm copies into a pinned buffer pool to avoid pageable copies, 3) run perfetto to catch CPU-side wakeups and verify scheduler spin behavior.

alex: I'm going to run a perfetto capture focused on CPU wakeups + futex/syscall patterns, then re-run nsys with nvtx ranges marking scheduler vs wrapper vs engine. Will share shortly.

jordan: also consider changing the wrapper to mark small prewarm ranges as a single NVTX range so the profiler groups them; helps the analysis. If pinned pool + batching don't fix it we might look at changing the prewarm heuristic to lazy-fill during generation.

maya: logged PERF-324: Reduce kvcache prewarm chatter across wrappers. Assigning to @alex and @jordan.

alex: noted and starting a follow-up run. Thanks all :thumbsup:
